**Geographic focus:**

**Temporal focus:**
T1. Historical report [NO]
T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES]
T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [NO]

**Synopsis:**
US military strikes on Iranian missile launchers in the Strait of Hormuz, combined with Iranian retaliatory attacks and threats to shipping lanes, have pushed Brent crude above $90/bbl and pressured global equities. Gulf oil exports remain well below pre-war levels despite partial recovery from the March trough. Against this inflationary backdrop, multiple central banks face near-term rate decisions — the Fed (58% hike probability Sep 16), ECB (high hike probability Sep 10), BoJ (70% hike probability Sep 18), RBNZ (certain hike), and BoC (hold expected). G20 finance ministers meet Monday–Tuesday in North Carolina, with tone expected to be hawkish. Key data: German CPI/HICP for August.

---

**Q01. Is the content relevant to US economy, US yields, US interest rates and US market pricing?**
Relevance: YES — Article directly references US equity futures (-0.4–0.5%), Treasury yield selloff, Fed rate decision probability, and the G20 meeting hosted in the US, all within the context of an oil shock.

**Q02. Is the content about increasing US interest rates?**
Relevance: 70 (moderately high — hawkish tone from oil prices and G20 narrative, Fed hike probability explicitly cited)
Probability of increase: 58%

**Q03. Is the content about holding stable US interest rates?**
Relevance: 30 (the hold scenario is implicitly the alternative to the cited 58% hike probability)
Probability of holding: 42%

**Q04. Is the content about decreasing US interest rates?**
Relevance: 0 (NO — no mention of rate cuts; the entire macro context — oil at $90, ongoing conflict, hawkish G20 tone — runs contrary to any easing narrative)
Probability of decrease: 0%

**Q05. Focus on the very latest information: What is the sentiment/tone including the very latest information on US interest rates?**
Sentiment: +65 (More hawkish than before) — Oil above $90, no resolution to the Gulf conflict, Friday's Treasury selloff extending into Monday, G20 expected to strike a hawkish tone, and markets now pricing a 58% chance the Fed hikes on Sep 16. All forward signals tilt toward tighter-for-longer conditions.
